english_verification.review_scope: Primary read actual current Mod names, representative history/formation/idea originals and fixed-revision English Wiki passages while completing the English text. Full research conclusions and scores remain inherited from the Chinese source; this is not an exhaustive mechanism audit.
unresolved: Wiki describes an ideology and later thought experiment, not a Z99 polity established in 1444.
Esthíl and other predecessors remain separate stories and do not automatically contribute their scores or mission counts.
Existing current-script research supplies the 92 definition count and harms; this translation does not perform exhaustive reachability or a new score review.

rationale.campaign_length: 92 direct Z99 missions; predecessor missions such as B54's are excluded.
rationale.colonization: The unique tree centres on continental conquest and magical engineering, not an overseas-colonial loop.
rationale.complexity: Formation rewards, Acolyte land allocation and laws, influence, succession, missions and research must be managed together.
rationale.dark_story: Legal second-class status, selective liberation and non-consensual research are explicit dark themes.
rationale.difficulty: Subjects and multiple campaign fronts require time and intensive management; the current balance was not quantified through playtesting.
rationale.diplomacy: Acolyte influence, succession and loyalty create complex internal diplomacy; external policy still relies mainly on conquest.
rationale.early_pressure: The predecessor must qualify through the Escanni Wars of Consolidation; integration and diplomatic pressures remain high after formation.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Mage government, magical duels, rituals, dragons, the Deepwoods and the World Tree's old roots permeate gameplay.
rationale.narrative_density: The post-consolidation Skull Throne leads into Acolytes, dragons, forest engineering and a nearly deified ruler in a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Research facilities, magical materials and Castonath construction matter, but serve larger-scale domination.
rationale.trade_economy: Subject tribute and magical resources matter, but commerce is not the strongest national identity.
rationale.warfare: The Escanni Wars of Consolidation gate formation; magical wars then expand into Cannor and beyond.

identity.appearance: Does not exist in 1444; a route reward after the Escanni Wars of Consolidation grants eligibility for a formation decision.
identity.formation_scope: Choosing the Black Demesne consolidation reward grants can_form_bd. B54, Z37, B53, B39 or a qualifying Witch-King ruler can then execute walk_the_stellar_path, switching to Z99, theocracy, Black Demesne culture and non-generic missions. Predecessor stories do not automatically become Z99 missions.
predecessors: Other Escanni countries meeting the formation reward and Witch-King conditions
identity.region: Escann → Cannor and beyond (formed in Escann, expanding across Cannor and farther afield)

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; excludes selectable idea groups and racial or government bonuses. Alternative sets and conditions are listed separately, not treated as simultaneous stacking. Adoption of new ideas on formation depends on the actual event or decision and player choice.

description.text: In the cosmology of the Black Doctrine, all beings with the capability to use magic are positioned somewhere in a great chain of ascension, sometimes called the 'Ascendant Path'. At the near end of this path are the so-called 'potentiates', people who have latent magical ability but lack the discipline to use it in any consistent and meaningful way. At the far end lies the Universal Mind, the great dispassionate, impersonal intellect which suffuses all the world. The Ascendant is the being who traverses this great path, growing in each stage until they achieve a true union with that purest Intellect. Officially, every Sorcerer-King was Ascendant, though any serious discussion with heretics will reveal that this is a point of much contention.

description.text: The Week of Ascension was simultaneously one of the world's most egalitarian institutions and one of its most stratified. Regardless of social class, all non-magical subjects participated in the same festivals and shared in the same activities during the seven-day celebration of virtue. However, every magic user was kept separate from these festivities, instead joining the Sorcerer-King in the Charred Tower for a week of celebration, debauchery, and furious politicking.

description.text: There have been various attempts to regulate and control magical research throughout the history of the mortal realms. Indeed, perhaps one of the truest signs of a healthy state has been its ability to impose at least some basic restrictions on the activities of mages. In the Black Demesne, to suggest such regulations was not merely seen as foolish, but rather a blasphemous heresy against Doctrine itself. Any law which restricted the development of Intellect was opposed to Doctrine, and restrictions on magic were the most heinous of these.

description.text: Though the non-magical classes could not ascend to the highest rungs of state power in the Demesne, and though they had very limited rights, they nonetheless rose in prominence. Precisely because the most powerful positions were restricted to magic users, these same powerful people often chose to surround themselves with those who could not possibly be a threat. They often promoted members of the non-magical class based on pure competence, justifying the high placement on the basis of intellectual virtue. This was in stark contrast to many other kingdoms, where promotion was by right of blood alone.

description.text: Undead are useful on the field of battle as brute soldiers, but they have very limited capacity to think for themselves or listen to verbal orders. Thus, the Demesne had great need for living scouts, battlefield engineers, and officers. Such positions were an excellent way for non-magical subjects to climb the social ladder by making themselves valuable to mages. Every time war was declared, a great influx of some of the Demesne's most intelligent, driven, and ambitious people came to serve the army in all manner of roles, a pattern that would later earn the moniker of 'the Reaper's Gift'.

description.text: In most societies, mages are typically reclusive academics who have little interest in battlefield glory, and only a smaller portion have the inclination to take up arms and lend their talents to the field of glory. In the Demesne, it was an expectation and personal obligation for every magical initiate to serve for at least some time in the military. This vastly greater pool of magical manpower allowed the Demesne to turn the entire upper officer corps into the exclusive province of mages, allowing decentralized and responsive magical tactics that were far more impressive than any single sorcerer could achieve alone.

description.text: At its greatest extent, the Black Demesne had eight Acolytes, each of whom wore an ebony ring, numbered from the First to the Eighth in order of magical prowess and prominence within the court. The Sorcerer-King wore a matching ring of dark gold, signifying dominance, which would become known as the Ninth ring. Theoretically, as long as one wore the ring of an Acolyte, one was honorbound to give nothing but absolute loyalty to the legitimate bearer of the Ninth ring in all matters. This reminder of hierarchy and control fortified the political order of the Demesne's upper class.

player_overview.avoid_if: You dislike managing many subjects and intensive long campaigns, or do not want to play a state that oppresses non-casters.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Win Escann as a predecessor; form the Demesne, establish Acolyte realms and arrange lands and succession, expand with mages and undead armies, then complete large arcane research projects.
player_overview.overview: The Black Demesne is not a 1444 starting country but a mage empire formable after winning the Escanni Wars of Consolidation. As Z99, train a mage ruler, establish and control competing Acolyte realms, and expand with undead armies. Its 92 unique missions lead towards dragons, the Deepwoods and vast magical projects. It values magical talent regardless of bloodline, yet gives non-magical people second-class legal status and advances research through involuntary experiments.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy dark mage narratives, extremely long mission trees, complex subject governance and cross-regional expansion.
signature_features: The Escanni consolidation reward determines formation eligibility; Esthíl is only one of several predecessor routes.
Acolyte realms distribute land through influence and laws, making mage competition central to imperial government.
Magical tournaments, dragons and engineering around the World Tree's old roots give the late campaign a personal Witch-King epic.
player_overview.tagline: Make mage privilege national law, then have the Acolytes conquer the world for the Skull Throne.

reasons: A distinctive Acolyte, influence and magical-election system
92 unique missions sustain an extremely long Witch-King epic
Different predecessors give the same formable different opening stories
warnings: The Escanni consolidation formation threshold is high.
Acolytes and expansion require sustained micromanagement.
The state openly oppresses non-casters and permits non-consensual research.

positive_indicators: Some appointments of casters escape hereditary bloodline restrictions.
Undead undertake some dangerous warfare, reducing the need for living soldiers.
Included casters can rise through the Acolyte system.
values.rationale: Conquest, theocracy and undead troops do not themselves incur a deduction. Appointing mages regardless of bloodline and substituting undead for living soldiers offer limited benefits. However, the reform legally subordinates non-casters; missions selectively free potential mages while permitting others to remain enslaved, and organise involuntary experiments on sapient fey. These directly violate dignity, personhood and restraint, placing the country in the Evil band.
red_flags: The government reform establishes comprehensive legal oppression of non-casters.
Supposed slave liberation targets only potential casters.
Sapient fey in the Deepwoods are described as involuntary research subjects.
